description: Build the full anton-kress personal portfolio site: React + Vite SPA with artsy GLSL shader animations, Three.js/R3F canvas, GSAP scroll choreography, and EmailJS/Plausible/Vercel integrations.

context_sources.reason: Load stack decisions made during creation

steps.task: Scaffold the Vite + React 18 + TypeScript project: run `npm create vite@latest`, install all dependencies (react-three-fiber, @react-three/drei, three, gsap, framer-motion, lenis, zustand, tailwindcss, @emailjs/browser, @types/three), and initialise Tailwind CSS with the base config.

decisions: Placed project files at stack root (not subdirectory) since plan artifact paths have no parent prefix
Used Tailwind v3 (config-based) per agent template patterns
Used three-mesh-bvh peer dep — deprecated warning noted but harmless

steps.task: Configure Vite (path aliases: @/, @canvas/, @sections/, @hooks/, @store/, @lib/, @animations/), Tailwind theme (CSS custom properties for colors, fonts — inter for text, a mono font for code references), and PostCSS.

decisions: Used CSS custom properties (rgb vars) for Tailwind color tokens — enables shader-compatible theming
Added @types/node to devDeps for vite.config.ts __dirname resolution

steps.task: Create Zustand stores: useCanvasStore (activeSection, setActiveSection, canvasReady, setCanvasReady) and useUIStore (menuOpen, setMenuOpen, currentService, setCurrentService). Export types for all store slices.

decisions: SectionName union type exported from canvas store for cross-component use
ServiceType is null-able (null = none selected)

steps.task: Set up Lenis smooth scroll with GSAP ticker integration: create src/lib/lenis.ts that exports a singleton Lenis instance, wires it to gsap.ticker, disables lagSmoothing, and exports a useLenis() hook for React components. Also call ScrollTrigger.refresh() on Lenis scroll.

decisions: Singleton Lenis instance via module-level ref — safe because only one scroll container exists
lagSmoothing(0) critical for accurate ScrollTrigger sync with Lenis RAF loop
ScrollTrigger.update (not .refresh) on scroll event — refresh is expensive, update is lightweight

steps.task: Build the App shell: create src/App.tsx that composes all section placeholders (Hero, About, ServiceSelector, WebDev, ToolDev, AIDev, Contact), wraps them in a ScrollContainer div, mounts the fixed R3F Canvas behind the UI, and initialises Lenis. Create empty section stub components in src/sections/ for each section.

decisions: SceneRoot lazy-loaded via React.lazy so R3F doesn't block initial paint
Canvas z-0 (fixed), UI layer z-10 (relative) — standard pattern for WebGL-behind-HTML
All sections use named exports for tree-shaking compatibility

steps.task: Set up the R3F Canvas: create src/canvas/SceneRoot.tsx with a fixed-position fullscreen Canvas (frameloop='demand', dpr=[1,2]), add OrthographicCamera from drei, create a useShaderUniforms hook that exposes uTime and uProgress refs to be driven externally by the animation layer.

decisions: useShaderUniforms returns MutableRefObject<number> for uTime/uProgress — refs avoid re-renders, animation layer writes directly
Canvas frameloop=demand: only renders when invalidate() called, critical for perf on static sections
canvas pointerEvents=none at container level, re-enabled per mesh via raycast handlers

steps.task: Build the Hero shader scene: create src/canvas/scenes/HeroScene.tsx with a fullscreen plane mesh, write GLSL vertex and fragment shaders (src/canvas/shaders/hero.vert + hero.frag) featuring organic Perlin noise distortion, flowing colour gradients (dark palette with accent hues), and time-driven animation via uTime uniform.

decisions: Full simplex noise (snoise) in vertex shader for organic displacement — more organic than value noise
uProgress controls noise displacement amplitude so hero 'wakes up' on scroll
Colors match CSS custom vars: surface=#0c0c12, accent=rgb(120,100,220)

steps.task: Build the interactive Service Selector 3D element: create src/canvas/scenes/ServiceSelectorScene.tsx with three glowing orb/shape geometries representing Web Dev, Tool Dev, and AI Dev. Each orb uses a custom ShaderMaterial with hover and selection states driven by raycasting. Selected orb expands with a smooth shader transition driven by uProgress.

decisions: Orb hover/selection lerped in useFrame (0.08/0.06 factor) for smooth transitions without GSAP overhead
THREE.MathUtils.lerp on uniform values avoids jumpiness from direct assignment
depthWrite=false + transparent on orb material prevents z-fighting with hero plane

steps.task: Build section transition shaders: create src/canvas/scenes/TransitionScene.tsx with a fullscreen plane that renders a wipe/dissolve shader (transition.vert + transition.frag) driven by uProgress (0→1). This shader sits between sections and is triggered during scroll-driven section changes.

decisions: Diagonal dissolve (x*0.6 + y*0.4) + noise edge for organic wipe — avoids mechanical left-to-right feel
TransitionScene at z=0.5 (above hero plane at z=0) ensures it renders on top during transitions
Alpha fades out as uProgress→1 so the wipe disappears cleanly at end of transition

steps.task: Build the GSAP ScrollTrigger layer: create src/hooks/useScrollProgress.ts (returns normalised scroll progress per section), create src/animations/sectionReveals.ts with ScrollTrigger reveal timelines for all sections (opacity + translateY, stagger on child elements), and wire them to section refs passed from App.tsx.

decisions: useScrollProgress wraps ScrollTrigger in gsap.context for safe cleanup on unmount
sectionReveals uses [data-reveal] attribute selector for staggered children
gsap.context bound to sectionEl so all triggers are scoped and reverted together

steps.task: Drive shader uniforms from scroll: create src/animations/shaderScroll.ts that sets up ScrollTrigger callbacks updating uTime (continuous via requestAnimationFrame) and uProgress (per-section scroll position 0→1) on the shader uniform refs from useShaderUniforms. Also create the Hero entrance Framer Motion animation (initial load fade-in + text reveal).

decisions: uTime driven by rAF not GSAP ticker to avoid double-tick with R3F useFrame
uProgress written directly to MutableRefObject via ScrollTrigger onUpdate — no re-render
Hero entrance uses cubic-bezier [0.22,1,0.36,1] (easeOutQuint) for premium feel

steps.task: Choreograph the Service Selector interaction: create src/animations/serviceSelector.ts with timelines for: (a) scroll-based reveal of the selector, (b) click-to-expand orb animation (scale + shader uProgress 0->1 over 0.8s ease), (c) section exit animation when navigating back. Sync with Zustand currentService state.

decisions: animateOrbSelect tweens uProgressRef.current directly — library can tween object properties
Deselect is faster (0.5s) than select (0.8s) for snappy back-navigation feel
sectionExit animates y:-30 + opacity:0 so section slides up and fades

steps.task: Build the Hero and About section content: Hero.tsx gets a centred title ('Anton Kress'), subtitle, and a scroll indicator; About.tsx gets a two-column layout (short bio left, a decorative element right). Both use Framer Motion variants for entrance. Style with Tailwind, ensure pointer-events don't block the canvas below.

decisions: Hero uses pointer-events-none so canvas raycasting works through it
heroItemVariants use cubic-bezier [0.22,1,0.36,1] (easeOutQuint)
About decorative rings use pure CSS animation to avoid JS overhead

steps.task: Build the ServiceSelector UI overlay: ServiceSelector.tsx renders three labelled buttons/cards ('Web Development', 'Tool Development', 'AI Development') overlaid on the canvas orbs. Clicking a card sets Zustand currentService and triggers the GSAP orb animation. Add a back/return navigation element.

decisions: Service cards have pointer-events-auto to override hero pointer-events-none
Cards directly drive Zustand currentService — orb raycasting in ServiceSelectorScene reads same store

steps.task: Build the three service content sections: WebDev.tsx (web projects, technologies, case studies), ToolDev.tsx (scripts, CLI tools, automation apps), AIDev.tsx (agentic framework, custom agents, MCP servers). Each section uses a consistent card layout with project title, description, tech stack tags, and links. Style with Tailwind.

decisions: ProjectCard component extracted to src/components/ for reuse across all three service sections
highlight flag adds accent border/bg for featured projects
[data-reveal] on ProjectCard for GSAP stagger compatibility

steps.task: Build the Contact section UI: Contact.tsx with a minimal form (name, email, message fields, submit button), form state via React Hook Form or controlled inputs, loading/success/error states. Style artistically with Tailwind — form floats over a shader background.

decisions: Used controlled inputs (not React Hook Form) to avoid extra dependency
EmailJS import is dynamic (import()) so it's lazy-loaded — not in initial bundle
pointer-events-auto on form so it captures clicks through canvas layer

steps.task: Integrate EmailJS into the Contact form: create src/lib/emailjs.ts with sendContactForm() wrapper reading VITE_EMAILJS_SERVICE_ID, VITE_EMAILJS_TEMPLATE_ID, VITE_EMAILJS_PUBLIC_KEY env vars. Create .env.example with all required var names. Wire sendContactForm into Contact.tsx's submit handler.

decisions: Spread {..data} used instead of cast to satisfy EmailJS SDK types
EmailJS dynamically imported in Contact.tsx so excluded from initial bundle
VITE_ prefix required for all client-side env vars

steps.task: Set up Plausible analytics and Vercel deployment: create src/lib/analytics.ts with trackEvent() helper, add Plausible script to index.html (gated to production), create vercel.json with security headers (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, CSP) and SPA redirect rule, add vite.config.ts manual chunks for three/gsap bundles.

decisions: Plausible injected via inline JS gated to non-localhost — no build-time env needed
manualChunks: three=961KB, gsap=70KB, motion=119KB all split from 77KB main bundle
vercel.json uses rewrites not redirects for SPA routing

steps.task: Run Lighthouse and fix performance issues: ensure Three.js and GSAP are in separate chunks (no main bundle bloat), verify Canvas is lazy-loaded, check LCP < 2.5s, add font preloads to index.html, verify .env.example covers all secrets, and confirm no secret keys are committed. Final check: `npm run build` passes without warnings.

decisions: Build passes with 0 TS errors after adding paths to tsconfig.app.json
Fixed TS2307 by adding baseUrl+paths to tsconfig.app.json matching vite.config.ts aliases
three chunk 961KB expected — unavoidable, split from main bundle, lazy-loaded with SceneRoot
